title: Open Legend — Art Direction, Round 02
status: Follow-up to 47 round-one ratings; all new ratings start empty

entries.title: Kathy Rain 2: Soothsayer
entries.focus: Readable outfits, adult proportions, atmospheric streets
entries.borrow: Following your praise for Tails Noir: inspect the people standing in the scene, their clothing layers, and colored light on wet surfaces.
entries.caution: A detailed dialogue portrait is visible too. Judge the smaller world figures separately; the city and mystery setting are not proposals.
entries.question: Do the world figures have enough face, clothing, and body detail—or does only the large portrait meet your target?

entries.title: Unavowed
entries.focus: Distinct people, clothing, and restrained material shading
entries.borrow: The cast has different builds, hairstyles, layers, and recognizable clothing. This tests the identity you want beyond Eastward’s simplified bodies.
entries.caution: Its adventure-game camera gives people much more screen space than an overhead simulation would. The large portrait is a separate artwork.
entries.question: Is this a useful target for ordinary people in the world, or does the finish still feel too old-fashioned?

images.label: World cast at right · dialogue portrait at left

entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: HUNTDOWN
entries.focus: Costume detail, dense materials, sharp local light
entries.borrow: Compare readable clothing and bodies against carefully drawn urban surfaces. This tests how much detail matters independently of the setting.
entries.caution: Exaggerated action poses and a deliberate arcade flavor may conflict with your preference for a contemporary finish.
entries.question: Do the sprites meet your detail threshold, and can you separate their craft from the retro action styling?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder
entries.focus: Layered foliage, textured machinery, expressive color
entries.borrow: A bridge from Owlboy’s environmental richness to taller action sprites. Look at light through foliage, depth layers, and material texture.
entries.caution: The hero remains small in gameplay; large anime dialogue portraits are shown only as a comparison, not evidence of world-sprite detail.
entries.question: Does the forest have the right richness? Are the actual world sprites detailed enough, independent of the portraits?

entries.title: The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow
entries.focus: Organic woodland, layered branches, ordinary clothing
entries.borrow: Moves the comparison out of neon cities: inspect irregular trees, undergrowth, atmospheric distance, and the clothing of people in a landscape.
entries.caution: Its folk-horror mood and visible pixel grain may be too gloomy or coarse. This is a wilderness/material study, not a horror recommendation.
entries.question: Would you want this kind of organic landscape with warmer daylight and finer characters, or is the pixel treatment itself unsuitable?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: The Last Faith
entries.focus: Long silhouettes, coats, gear, and intricate architecture
entries.borrow: Follows your positive reaction to Blasphemous 2’s legible gear. Study equipment and clothing shapes alongside detailed surfaces.
entries.caution: Gothic gloom and combat are not the target. Rate the character and material definition separately from the oppressive atmosphere.
entries.question: Is this closer to the clothing and equipment fidelity you want, if placed in a more inviting world?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: Chrono Sword
entries.focus: Oblique view, depth, textured ground, local light
entries.borrow: Tests the hardest translation: bringing atmospheric pixel scenery into an angled view while keeping individual agents legible.
entries.caution: The small cloaked figure has less facial and clothing information than a side-view adventure cast. Do not treat scene detail as proof of character detail.
entries.question: Does this camera and ground treatment appeal? How much larger or more finely drawn would the people need to be?

images.label: Angled gameplay view · world figure and environment

entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: NORCO
entries.focus: Wetland atmosphere, reflective water, layered vegetation
entries.borrow: An environment-only study following your interest in Ferrari’s water and Rocha’s wilderness composition.
entries.caution: Scenes and close-up artwork are not ordinary simulation sprites. The industrial melancholy may not be the emotional target.
entries.question: Would you borrow its atmosphere and landscape texture, with more warmth and visible life?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: Savior
entries.focus: Expressive motion, clouds, organic fantasy forms
entries.borrow: Explore animation and a brighter fantasy palette as a counterweight to the darker detail studies. Source article includes motion footage.
entries.caution: Historical promotional artwork. The small hero and stylized creatures may still be too simplified; this is not presented as a proven character-detail match.
entries.question: Does the sense of life and motion appeal, even if the shapes or pixels need more definition?

entries.title: Death’s Gambit: Afterlife
entries.focus: Readable equipment and fantasy environment texture
entries.borrow: A further test of the gear visibility you liked in Blasphemous 2, alongside foliage, stone, and atmospheric color.
entries.caution: Small action sprites and stylized fantasy shapes may still fall below your desired density. Separate the gear study from dark-fantasy subject matter.
entries.question: Does this equipment read clearly enough, or do you want subtler, finer anatomy and material detail?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: Beyond the Ice Palace 2
entries.focus: Tall armored figures, stonework, layered backgrounds
entries.borrow: Another equipment-and-material comparison: assess shape separation, highlights on clothing or armor, and definition within the scenery.
entries.caution: Its nostalgic platformer presentation may feel dated despite detailed drawing. This intentionally tests that boundary.
entries.question: Is the character craftsmanship useful, or does the overall retro finish make it the wrong direction?

entries.title: Whispers of a Machine
entries.focus: Natural proportions and a more restrained color range
entries.borrow: Compare human scale, clothing silhouettes, and everyday environments with the more theatrical lighting of Kathy Rain 2 and Unavowed.
entries.caution: It may read too muted or too much like a classic adventure game. A quieter palette is being tested, not prescribed.
entries.question: Does the restraint make the people and materials more convincing, or does it lose the richness you want?
entries.reuse: Reference only. Images remain at credited hosts; no production asset rights acquired.

entries.title: The Drifter
entries.focus: Natural human silhouettes with conspicuous pixel grain
entries.borrow: Useful for separating anatomy and mood from raw pixel density. The office scene gives people recognizable clothing and posture.
entries.caution: The pixels remain quite visible and the faces small. This is a lower-detail comparison rather than a claim that it matches REPLACED.
entries.question: Are these bodies and outfits convincing enough despite the grain, or is this clearly below your minimum density?

entries.title: VirtuaVerse
entries.focus: Dense props and strongly colored light
entries.borrow: Pushes the detailed urban-material side of Tails Noir toward a more intense palette. Consider the amount of visual information in a room or street.
entries.caution: Neon saturation may repeat your objection to UNSIGHTED. No cyberpunk setting is implied.
entries.question: Is the density appealing but the palette too much, or do both work when the lighting is this deliberate?

entries.title: Tower 57
entries.focus: Overhead character readability and dense props
entries.borrow: An overhead counterpart to the taller side-view references: inspect costumes, body distinctions, material texture, and walkable-space clarity.
entries.caution: The exaggerated proportions and retro flavor may be a mismatch. This tests the camera/detail trade-off rather than proposes its entire style.
entries.question: Can an overhead view like this preserve enough individuality, or does it make people too small and cartoon-like?

entries.title: ANNO: Mutationem

entries.caution: Explicit 2D/3D hybrid and anime styling. These may be exactly what you do not want; this is a narrowly labeled boundary test.
entries.question: Does the character detail change your view of a hybrid presentation, or is the visual mismatch still a clear no?
